output.text_response:
# Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Ireland (1780–1870)

## Jurisdiction Overview

- **Civil parish:** Billy, barony of Carey and barony of Lower Dunluce, County Antrim, Ulster
- **Local post-town:** Bushmills
- **Denominations confirmed:** Presbyterian (dominant), Covenanters (Reformed Presbyterian), Wesleyan Methodist, Church of Ireland, Roman Catholic (filed under the RC district of Coleraine — *not* under Billy)
- **Key events:** 1798 United Irishmen rebellion; Great Famine 1845–1852; 1922 partition (records split between PRONI/Belfast and Dublin)

---

## Civil Registration

| Event | Start date |
|---|---|
| Protestant marriages | 1845 |
| All births, deaths, marriages | 1864 |

**Gap:** Civil registration covers only the final years of the 1780–1870 window. Church registers are the primary source for 1780–1863.

**Where held:** General Register Office Northern Ireland (GRONI) — [nidirect.gov.uk/gro](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/gro)

---

## Church Records (the Core Gap-Filler)

### Presbyterian

- Two FamilySearch browse-only volumes for Ballylinny/Billy area:
  - **Christenings 1837–1868** (image group 007907410_008\_M9VF-SK5, 65 images) — full-text searchable, **0% name-indexed** (must be browsed by text, not name search)
  - **Marriage Records 1837–1864** (image group 007765074_009\_M9VX-Q7W, 50 images) — same limitation
- PRONI holds microfilm MIC 1P/327 (1851 onward); FamilySearch Library film 973220 covers 1837 onward
- **Gap 1780–1836:** No digitized Presbyterian register confirmed for this earlier span. Original registers may be in custody of the local congregation.

### Church of Ireland

- Billy was head of an ecclesiastical union comprising Armoy, Ballyclug, Donegore, and Kilbride (Archdeaconry of Connor, Diocese of Connor).
- **Major loss:** Two-thirds of Church of Ireland registers were destroyed in the 1922 Public Record Office fire in Dublin. What survives for Billy specifically is unconfirmed by any tool result. **Check PRONI and the RCB Library first** before assuming registers are lost.

### Roman Catholic

- Billy civil parish falls within the **RC district of Coleraine** (Diocese of Down and Connor). Search Catholic records under *Coleraine*, not *Billy*.
- Most rural Catholic registers didn't begin until after Emancipation (c. 1828).
- **Gap 1780–c.1828:** Catholic registers for this district likely don't predate the late 1820s–1830s.

### Covenanter (Reformed Presbyterian) and Methodist

- Meeting houses confirmed for Billy parish but **no digitized registers found** in this survey. Consult PRONI Guide to Church Records.

---

## Census and Census Substitutes

| Record | Years | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Tithe Applotment Books | 1823–1837 | Names heads of household by townland; free at [irishgenealogy.ie](https://www.irishgenealogy.ie) |
| Griffith's Primary Valuation | 1848–1864 | Names all property occupiers; free at [askaboutireland.ie](https://www.askaboutireland.ie); also on Ancestry |
| Valuation Revision Books (Ballylinny/Billy) | 1867–1881 | FamilySearch image group 004689599 (76 images, browse only) |
| Irish censuses | 1861, 1871, 1881, 1891 | **Destroyed** — do not exist |
| Census fragments 1841–1851 | Partial | Survive mainly as Old Age Pension evidence; survival for Billy unconfirmed |

---

## Other Key Record Types

- **School records:** Deffrick National School Girls (FamilySearch image group 008682995\_005\_M94W-68Y), April 1867–1933 — touches the tail end of the target window
- **Marriage License Bonds 1623–1866:** FamilySearch collection [Ireland, Diocesan and Prerogative Marriage License Bonds Indexes](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3460239) — partial substitute for destroyed church records
- **Probate (pre-1858):** Mostly destroyed 1922; surviving abstracts on FindMyPast (Betham, Crossle, Thrift collections)
- **Newspapers:** Belfast News-Letter (from 1737); Coleraine Chronicle (from 1844) — obituaries, marriage notices — at British Newspaper Archive (subscription)

---

## Repository Guide

### Online

| Repository | What it holds for Billy / County Antrim | Access |
|---|---|---|
| **FamilySearch** familysearch.org | Presbyterian christenings & marriages 1837–1868; valuation 1867–1881; school records 1867+; marriage license bonds 1623–1866 | Free |
| **PRONI Digitised Church Records** nidirect.gov.uk/articles/digitised-church-records-available-proni | Church register microfilms for all denominations; download the [Guide to Church Records (PDF)](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf) | Free |
| **National Library of Ireland Catholic Registers** registers.nli.ie | Digitized Catholic parish registers (search under Coleraine district) | Free |
| **IrishGenealogy.ie** irishgenealogy.ie | Tithe Applotment Books; some civil registration | Free |
| **Ancestry** ancestry.com | Ireland, Catholic Parish Registers, 1655–1915; Griffith's Valuation; Irish Records Index 1500–1920 | Subscription |
| **FindMyPast** findmypast.com | Non-Conformist Births/Marriages/Burials; Betham, Crossle & Thrift Abstracts (destroyed probate); Church of Ireland Ffolliott Collection | Subscription |
| **RootsIreland** (Ulster Historical Foundation) rootsireland.ie / ancestryireland.com | Transcription index for Ulster church records (multiple denominations) | Subscription |
| **British Newspaper Archive** britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk | Belfast News-Letter, Coleraine Chronicle, other Ulster papers | Subscription |

### Physical Repositories

| Repository | Address | Key holdings | Contact |
|---|---|---|---|
| **PRONI** | 2 Titanic Boulevard, Titanic Quarter, Belfast BT3 9HQ | Church register microfilms (all denominations); estate records; valuation; civil registration NI; wills post-1858 | proni@communities-ni.gov.uk · 028 9053 4800 |
| **RCB Library** (Church of Ireland) | Braemor Park, Churchtown, Dublin 14, D14 N735 | Surviving CoI parish registers; list of all surviving registers at [ireland.anglican.org](https://www.ireland.anglican.org/cmsfiles/pdf/AboutUs/library/registers/ParishRegisters/PARISHREGISTERS.pdf) | library@ireland.anglican.org · +353 (0)1 492 3979 · [store.ireland.anglican.org/genealogy](https://store.ireland.anglican.org/genealogy) |
| **National Archives of Ireland** | Bishop Street, Dublin D08 DF85 | Tithe Applotment Books; National School registers; census fragments | nationalarchives.ie · mail@nationalarchives.ie |
| **GRONI** | — | Civil registration (marriages from 1845; births/deaths from 1864) | nidirect.gov.uk/gro |
| **Local Presbyterian congregations** | Bushmills area | Original registers in custody of local church | Direct contact |

---

## Known Record Losses

- **1922 PRO fire (Dublin):** Two-thirds of Church of Ireland registers destroyed; most pre-1922 wills and ecclesiastical probate destroyed
- **Irish censuses 1861–1891:** Destroyed by government order
- **British Army service records (pre-1920):** Large proportion destroyed in 1940 Arnside Street fire (London)

---

## Recommended Next Steps to Close Church-Register Gaps

1. **Download PRONI's Guide to Church Records** ([PDF](https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf)) to identify every congregation in Billy parish and what registers survive on microfilm.
2. **Contact PRONI** (proni@communities-ni.gov.uk) to verify what Church of Ireland, Covenanter, and Methodist registers are held for Billy, including any that predate 1837.
3. **Check the RCB Library** ([store.ireland.anglican.org/genealogy](https://store.ireland.anglican.org/genealogy)) for surviving Church of Ireland registers specific to Billy before concluding they were lost in 1922.
4. **Search Catholic registers under Coleraine** at [registers.nli.ie](https://www.registers.nli.ie) and on Ancestry (collection 61039) to establish actual coverage dates.
5. **Browse the two FamilySearch Presbyterian volumes** (image groups 007907410_008 and 007765074_009) using full-text search rather than name browse — they will not appear in a standard name search.
6. **Contact the local Presbyterian congregation** in Bushmills directly for any pre-1837 registers still in church custody.

# Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Ireland (1780-1870)

## Jurisdiction overview

- **Civil parish:** Billy, barony of Carey and barony of Lower Dunluce, County Antrim, province of Ulster
- **County seat / administrative centre:** Antrim town (County Antrim); local post-town within the parish is Bushmills
- **Parent jurisdiction:** County Antrim, Ireland (pre-1921); County Antrim, Northern Ireland, United Kingdom (post-1922)
- **Population during period:** Population data was not returned by the survey tools for this civil parish; no figures are cited here.
- **Economy:** North Antrim coastal and agricultural area; whiskey distilling at Bushmills throughout the period
- **Religious denominations:** Presbyterian (dominant), Covenanters (Reformed Presbyterian), Wesleyan Methodists, Church of Ireland, Roman Catholic (part of Coleraine district). The FamilySearch Wiki page for Billy civil parish names meeting houses for Presbyterians, Covenanters, and Wesleyan Methodists and places Roman Catholics within the RC district of Coleraine. (Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Billy_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy)
- **Key historical events:** 1798 United Irishmen rebellion affected Ulster broadly; Famine (1845-1852) caused severe population loss and emigration across Ireland including County Antrim; partition of Ireland in 1922 split the county's administrative records between PRONI (Belfast) and national bodies in Dublin.

## Boundary changes

- Billy was formerly the head of an ecclesiastical union that comprised Armoy, Ballyclug, Donegore, and Kilbride, together forming the corps of the Archdeaconry of Connor. That union affects which church registers are filed together.
- Civil and ecclesiastical boundaries do not align: Roman Catholics in the civil parish of Billy were served by the RC district of Coleraine, whose registers and boundaries differ from the Church of Ireland civil-parish boundary. When searching Catholic records, search under Coleraine, not Billy.
- After 1922, County Antrim remained in Northern Ireland (United Kingdom). Records created before 1922 survive in both PRONI (Belfast) and, where duplicates or indexes were held, in Dublin repositories. Records created after 1922 are held exclusively by Northern Ireland institutions.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)

- **Start dates (from the Billy Civil Parish FamilySearch Wiki page):** Government registration of births and deaths began 1864. Registration of Protestant marriages began 1845. All marriages were registered from 1864. (Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Billy_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy)
- **What exists:** Civil registers from 1845 (Protestant marriages) and 1864 (births, deaths, all marriages). These post-date most of the 1780-1870 target window, so they cover only the final years of the period.
- **Where held:** General Register Office Northern Ireland (GRONI). Access through PRONI's reading room or through irishgenealogy.ie for some years; for Northern Ireland records, the primary online route is the GRONI search at nidirect.gov.uk/gro.
- **Gaps:** Civil registration covers only 1845-1870 at best within the target window; the entire 1780-1844 span has no civil registration, and 1845-1863 covers only Protestant marriages.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Church registers are the primary source for 1780-1864 (see Church records section below).

### Church records

Church registers are the primary evidence for virtually the entire 1780-1870 target window. The FamilySearch Wiki Ireland Church Records page (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records) confirms: before civil registration (1864), church records provide the primary source for baptisms, marriages, and burials; Catholic and Presbyterian registers frequently do not contain burial registers.

#### Church of Ireland

- Billy was formerly the head of an ecclesiastical union comprising Armoy, Ballyclug, Donegore, and Kilbride, all forming the Archdeaconry of Connor (Diocese of Connor). The rectory and vicarage of Billy alone now constitute the corps of the archdeaconry.
- **Known gap and loss:** The Ireland Church Records wiki page states that two-thirds of Church of Ireland registers were destroyed in the 1922 Public Record Office fire in Dublin. What survives for Billy specifically (registers, copies, or Bishop's Transcripts) is not confirmed by any tool result in this survey. No digitized Church of Ireland volume for Billy was returned by the volume search.
- **To determine what survives for Billy specifically:** Contact the RCB Library (Representative Church Body Library), which holds surviving Church of Ireland registers, and PRONI, which holds microfilm copies of some Ulster registers. The RCB Library's printed list of parish registers, available at the URL below, names surviving registers with their date ranges:
  - **RCB Library:** Braemor Park, Churchtown, Dublin 14, D14 N735, Ireland. Tel: +353 (0)1 492 3979. Email: library@ireland.anglican.org. Request a search: https://store.ireland.anglican.org/genealogy. List of Parish Registers (PDF listing all surviving registers and their locations): https://www.ireland.anglican.org/cmsfiles/pdf/AboutUs/library/registers/ParishRegisters/PARISHREGISTERS.pdf
  - **PRONI:** 2 Titanic Boulevard, Titanic Quarter, Belfast, BT3 9HQ, Northern Ireland. Tel: 028 9053 4800. Email: proni@communities-ni.gov.uk. PRONI Guide to Church Records (names which churches existed in each parish and which records survive on microfilm or in original form): https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf. PRONI Digitised Church Records online: https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/digitised-church-records-available-proni#toc-1
- **Digitization level:** No Church of Ireland volume for Billy was returned by this survey's volume search. Access method is unknown until PRONI or the RCB Library is consulted.

#### Presbyterian

- Meeting houses for Presbyterians (and separately for Covenanters/Reformed Presbyterians) are confirmed for Billy parish.
- **What exists digitized at FamilySearch:** Two volumes for the Ballylinny/Billy area, returned by the volume search:
  - Christenings 1837-1868 (image group 007907410_008_M9VF-SK5, 65 images): full-text searchable but NOT name-indexed. Must be searched by text, not by name browse.
  - Marriage Records 1837-1864 (image group 007765074_009_M9VX-Q7W, 50 images): full-text searchable but NOT name-indexed.
- **Physical copies:** The FamilySearch Wiki search result for the Ballylinny area notes that microfilm copies are held at PRONI (film MIC 1P/327, covering 1851 onwards) and the original register is in the custody of the local church, with FamilySearch Library film 973220 covering baptisms and marriages from 1837. (Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ballylinny_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy#Church_records)
- **Gap 1780-1836:** No digitized Presbyterian register for Billy parish covering this period was returned by this survey. For records before 1837, the Ireland Church Records wiki page notes that the average starting date for Presbyterian registers in Ireland is 1830 and that numerous registers date from the 1600s, but existence of pre-1837 registers for Billy specifically is unconfirmed by tool results.
- **Gap: Covenanters (Reformed Presbyterian):** The existence and location of any surviving registers for the Covenanter congregation in Billy is not confirmed by any tool result in this survey. PRONI should be consulted; they hold the PRONI Guide to Church Records that covers all denominations.
- **FindMyPast** holds an "Ireland, Non-Conformist Births & Baptisms," "Ireland, Non-Conformist Marriages," and "Ireland, Non-Conformist Burials" index (subscription required): https://www.findmypast.com (search the Non-Conformist Congregational Records collection for Presbyterian entries).

#### Catholic

- Billy civil parish falls within the Roman Catholic district of Coleraine (Diocese of Connor and Down, now Diocese of Down and Connor). Catholic registers are filed under Coleraine, not under Billy.
- **What exists online:** The National Library of Ireland hosts digitized Catholic parish registers at https://registers.nli.ie. The Ancestry collection "Ireland, Catholic Parish Registers, 1655-1915" (index and images, subscription) at https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/61039/ covers many Antrim parishes.
- **Start date for Coleraine Catholic registers:** The Ireland Church Records wiki notes that most rural Irish parishes did not start keeping records until Catholic Emancipation in 1828; many city registers date from the 1750s. The specific start date for the Coleraine Catholic registers covering Billy was not confirmed in this survey's tool results. Consult registers.nli.ie or Ancestry to check coverage.
- **Gap 1780-circa 1828:** Catholic registers for the Coleraine district likely do not begin until the late 1820s or 1830s. No tool result confirmed an earlier start for Billy's RC district.
- **RootsIreland index** (Ulster Historical Foundation): paid transcription index at https://www.rootsireland.ie. The Ireland Church Records wiki notes that the Ulster Historical Foundation (https://www.ancestryireland.com) has indexed records including Catholic registers, and that Ballyclare Catholic records (a neighbouring area) were indexed by the Ulster Historical Foundation.
- **FindMyPast** also holds "Ireland Roman Catholic Parish Marriages" (subscription): https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/ireland-roman-catholic-parish-marriages

#### Methodist (Wesleyan)

- A Wesleyan Methodist meeting house is confirmed for Billy parish.
- **What exists:** No digitized Methodist volume for Billy was returned by the volume search. FindMyPast holds "Ireland, Non-Conformist Congregational Records" and related non-conformist collections (subscription): https://www.findmypast.com.
- PRONI's Guide to Church Records covers Methodist congregations in Ulster and should be consulted for Billy's specific congregation: https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf

### Census records

- **Irish census record losses:** The Irish census records for 1861, 1871, 1881, and 1891 were destroyed by order of the Irish government during World War I. The 1901 and 1911 censuses survive in full and are online at the National Archives of Ireland (nationalarchives.ie) and at FindMyPast. The 1841 and 1851 censuses survive only in fragments — head-of-household summary forms, some used as evidence in Old Age Pension claims. The Billy Civil Parish FamilySearch Wiki page redirects to the Ireland Census article for further information.
- **Practical result for 1780-1870:** No surviving national census covers this period in useful detail for Billy parish. The 1841 fragments are the only census-type records from the target window, and survival for Billy specifically is unconfirmed.
- **Substitute enumerations:** Griffith's Valuation (1848-1864) and the Tithe Applotment Books (1823-1837) function as the nearest census equivalents for this period (see Tax records below).

### Probate and court records

- **Pre-1858:** Probate was handled by ecclesiastical courts. For Billy, this was the Prerogative Court of Armagh (for high-value estates) and the Consistorial Court of Connor (the local diocesan court). Most of these records were destroyed in the 1922 PRO fire. The FamilySearch collection "Ireland, Diocesan and Prerogative Marriage License Bonds Indexes, 1623-1866" at FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3460239) covers marriage license bonds from the ecclesiastical courts and partially compensates.
- Betham Genealogical Abstracts (abstracts of wills and other records collected before the 1922 fire) are at FindMyPast: https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/betham-genealogical-abstracts. Thrift Genealogical Abstracts (including wills and parish register abstracts): https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/thrift-genealogical-abstracts.
- **Post-1858:** Civil district probate registries took over. PRONI holds probate records for Northern Ireland.
- The Billy Civil Parish FamilySearch Wiki page redirects to the Ireland Probate Records article for further detail.

### Land records

- **Survey system:** Metes and bounds with townland subdivisions. The civil parish of Billy is divided into townlands — the volume search confirmed the townland of Ballylinny as one subdivision.
- **Tithe Applotment Books (1823-1837):** A tithe assessment of land, naming heads of household for each townland. Functions as a near-census substitute for the 1820s-1830s. Available free at IrishGenealogy.ie and also at the NAI.
- **Griffith's Primary Valuation (1848-1864):** A comprehensive survey of all property occupiers in Ireland. The volume search returned a browse-only valuation volume for Ballylinny/Billy (VAL 12B/1/7B, 1867-1881, image group 004689599, 76 images) covering the later revision period. The original Griffith's survey is searchable free at askaboutireland.ie and at the subscription site Ancestry (Ireland, Griffith's Valuation, 1847-1864).
- **Estate records:** Large estates in County Antrim generated tenant records, leases, and rentals now held primarily at PRONI.
- The Billy Civil Parish FamilySearch Wiki page redirects to the Ireland Land and Property article.

### Military records

- **Relevant conflicts in the period:** United Irishmen rebellion 1798; Napoleonic Wars (service in British Army and Militia); Crimean War 1853-1856.
- British Army service records and pension records are held at The National Archives (UK), Kew, London (nationalarchives.gov.uk). Many pre-1920 service records were destroyed in the 1940 Arnside Street fire in London.
- Muster rolls, militia records, and some pension records for Ireland are at PRONI.
- The Fold3 platform (https://www.fold3.com, subscription) holds some British military records for the period.

### Cemetery records

- **Online:** FindAGrave (https://www.findagrave.com) has crowdsourced headstone entries for many County Antrim cemeteries. BillionGraves is a secondary option.
- **Physical:** The Ireland Church Records wiki notes that burials were typically recorded in church burial registers; Catholic and Presbyterian registers frequently do not contain burial registers. Sexton records and graveyard transcription projects (some held at PRONI or the North of Ireland Family History Society) may supplement.

### Newspaper records

- The principal paper covering north Antrim in this period was the Coleraine Chronicle (founded 1844) and the Belfast News-Letter (founded 1737, available in digitized form at the British Newspaper Archive: https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk, subscription). Obituaries, marriage notices, and legal notices are the genealogical content of most value.
- The British Newspaper Archive is the main online repository for digitized Irish and Ulster provincial newspapers of this period.

### Immigration and emigration records

- North Antrim was a major emigration area throughout 1780-1870, particularly to North America. Passenger lists (arrival manifests) are at NARA (US) and are indexed on Ancestry and FamilySearch.
- Emigration records specific to Ireland (sailings from Belfast, Londonderry, and Dublin) are held at PRONI and partially digitized.
- Note: Passenger lists record every person aboard, including infants and children traveling with parents. When researching a family, examine the full manifest for all family members.

### Tax records

- **Tithe Applotment Books 1823-1837:** Names heads of household for each townland in Billy. Available free at IrishGenealogy.ie and at NAI.
- **Griffith's Primary Valuation (1848-1864):** Names all property occupiers. See Land records above.
- **Revision Books (post-Griffith's):** Annual revision of Griffith's survives as the Valuation Office Books, held by the Valuation Office. The browse-only volume VAL 12B/1/7B (1867-1881) at FamilySearch covers the Ballylinny area of Billy parish.
- **Substitute value:** The tithe books (1823s-1830s) and Griffith's (1848-1864) together provide near-census coverage for the decades when no census survives.

### Other record types

- **School records:** One digitized but browse-only volume exists at FamilySearch for the period just touching the target window: Deffrick National School Girls (image group 008682995_005_M94W-68Y), covering April 1867-September 1933, 50 images. National school admission registers began after the National School system was established in 1831 and are held at the National Archives of Ireland.
- **Street directories and almanacs:** Pigot's (1824), Slater's (from 1846), and Bassett's directories name tradespeople and significant inhabitants in Bushmills and surrounding towns.
- **Estate and landlord records:** PRONI holds extensive estate records for County Antrim landlords that name tenants not found in any other source.

## Records NOT online

- **Church of Ireland registers for Billy parish:** No digitized Church of Ireland volume for Billy was returned by this survey. Survival after the 1922 fire is unconfirmed; physical access through PRONI or the RCB Library is required to establish what exists.
- **Covenanter (Reformed Presbyterian) registers for Billy:** No digitized volume found. Consult PRONI Guide to Church Records.
- **Wesleyan Methodist registers for Billy:** No digitized volume found. Consult PRONI Guide to Church Records.
- **Catholic registers for the Coleraine district before circa 1828:** Even where registers survive, early volumes for rural Catholic parishes may not yet be digitized. Confirm coverage dates at registers.nli.ie before concluding a gap exists.
- **Presbyterian registers before 1837:** The two FamilySearch volumes begin in 1837. Earlier registers, if any survive, have not been confirmed as online.
- **Estate and landlord tenant records:** Held at PRONI; largely not digitized online.
- **Probate records pre-1922 (ecclesiastical court series):** Mostly destroyed in 1922; surviving abstracts on FindMyPast partially compensate.

---

## Known record losses

- **1922 Public Record Office fire, Dublin:** The Ireland Church Records FamilySearch Wiki page (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records) states that two-thirds of Church of Ireland registers were destroyed in the 1922 PRO fire. Pre-1922 wills and many ecclesiastical court probate records were also destroyed. Surviving abstracts (Betham, Crossle, Thrift — all on FindMyPast) are partial substitutes.
- **Irish census records 1861-1891:** Destroyed (see Census records above). No tool result names any Billy-specific census material that survives.
- **British Army service records:** A large proportion of pre-1920 service records were destroyed in the 1940 Arnside Street fire in London.

---

## Research tips

- The FamilySearch Wiki page for Billy Civil Parish (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Billy_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy) gives the ecclesiastical union history and civil registration dates. The church records subsections of that page contain no register-specific detail — use it for context only and go directly to PRONI and the RCB Library for register information.
- The Ireland Church Records wiki page (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records) advises: search all parish registers of the appropriate locality for the time period; search available Church of Ireland records even if the family was not Church of Ireland; search surrounding parishes if records are not found in the expected locality, since Catholics had different parish boundaries from the Church of Ireland. For Billy, the Catholic boundary runs to the Coleraine RC district, not to the Church of Ireland civil parish boundary.
- The two FamilySearch digitized volumes for the Ballylinny/Billy area (christenings 1837-1868 and marriages 1837-1864) are **full-text searchable but carry a 0% name-index**. They will not appear in a standard record search by name. Use FamilySearch's full-text search interface, or browse them image-by-image, to find entries.
- The 1922 fire destroyed most original Church of Ireland registers held in Dublin. For north Antrim parishes, the first check should be PRONI (which holds microfilm copies of many Ulster registers) using their Guide to Church Records, before concluding a register was lost. Download PRONI's Guide at https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf.
- Griffith's Valuation (1848-1864) and the Tithe Applotment Books (1823-1837) together are the practical census substitutes for 1780-1864. Both survive for Billy's townlands and are largely free to access online.
- Note that FamilySearch's wiki place-pages for County Antrim at the getting-started, online-records, and research-tips section levels returned only generic content during this survey — they did not supply Ireland- or County Antrim-specific guidance. The FamilySearch wiki pages at https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records and https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Billy_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy did return substantive content and are the primary wiki sources for this guide.

---

Billy civil parish in County Antrim (pre-1922 Ireland) contains the town of Bushmills and was a predominantly Presbyterian and Nonconformist area, though Catholics and Church of Ireland families also lived there. For roughly the first eighty-five years of the target window (1780-1864), no civil registration existed, so church registers — Presbyterian, Church of Ireland, Roman Catholic, Covenanter, and Methodist — are the only source of baptism, marriage, and burial records. Two Presbyterian volumes for the Ballylinny area of the parish survive at FamilySearch (christenings 1837-1868 and marriages 1837-1864), but they cannot be searched by name; they must be browsed by text. The most important practical step for closing church-register gaps is to consult PRONI in Belfast and the RCB Library in Dublin, both of which hold surviving registers or microfilm copies that are not yet online, and to check the Catholic registers for the Coleraine district at the National Library of Ireland's free portal (registers.nli.ie) and at Ancestry.

The next step is to contact PRONI (proni@communities-ni.gov.uk) to request their Guide to Church Records for Billy parish, check the RCB Library's list of surviving Church of Ireland registers for Billy, and then search the Catholic registers at registers.nli.ie under the Coleraine district to establish what years of church-register coverage are actually available before planning record searches.

- Heavy immigration from Wales, Ireland, and German-speaking regions for the coal industry
- **Pre-1906 naturalizations** were filed at the county court (Court of Common Pleas), **not federal court** — check Schuylkill County courthouse; not confirmed online

# Locality Guide: Pulaski County, Kentucky (1840–1880)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** December 10, 1798, from Lincoln and Green counties
- **County seat:** Somerset
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Kentucky
- **Population during period:** Population figures were not returned by survey tools for this period
- **Economy:** Subsistence agriculture; small-scale trade along the Cumberland River
- **Ethnic composition:** Predominantly Scots-Irish and English-descent settlers; small free Black population
- **Religious denominations:** Baptist, Methodist, Roman Catholic, Presbyterian — the dominant groups in Kentucky before 1900 (Kentucky Church Records wiki: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Church_Records)
- **Key historical events:** Record losses in disasters in 1838 and again in 1871; Civil War (1861–1865) divided the county between Union and Confederate service

## Boundary changes
- Pulaski County was formed in 1798 from Lincoln and Green counties; records for Pulaski County residents before 1798 may be found in those parent jurisdictions
- No further boundary changes during the 1840–1880 period were returned by survey tools; boundaries were stable during the target period

## Available record types

Record types are held at the county level unless otherwise stated.

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start dates and what exists:** County-level birth and death registration began in 1853, with gaps — three intermittent periods: 1853–1862, 1874–1878, and 1892–1910, all with poor compliance. Marriages were recorded at the county level from county formation (1799). Statewide births and deaths began 1911; statewide marriages began 1958. (Kentucky Vital Records wiki: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Vital_Records)
- **Where held:** Pre-1911 records at the Pulaski County Courthouse and the Kentucky Department for Libraries and Archives (KDLA), Frankfort; statewide records from 1911 at the Kentucky Office of Vital Statistics
- **Gaps:** Large portions of the 1840–1880 target period fall outside any registration window (1862–1874 and 1878–1892 have no county-level birth or death registration); compliance was poor even within the open windows; some records lost in the 1838 and 1871 disasters; marriage bonds and consent forms 1799–1871 are digitized on FamilySearch; church records, mortality schedules, and cemetery records are the primary substitutes for missing vital events

### Church records
- **Denominations and online access:** Baptist, Methodist, Roman Catholic, and Presbyterian were the dominant denominations. FamilySearch holds: Kentucky Church Records, 1818–1995 (index and images, incomplete); Kentucky Births and Christenings, 1839–1960 (index only); Kentucky Marriages, 1785–1979 (index only); Kentucky Deaths and Burials, 1843–1970 (index only). (Kentucky Church Records wiki: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Church_Records)
- **Roman Catholic records:** Kentucky is divided among four Catholic dioceses — Covington, Lexington, Louisville, and Owensboro. Which diocese covers Pulaski County is unconfirmed by this survey; contact the Diocese of Lexington and the Diocese of Louisville for Pulaski County sacramental registers
- **Physical repositories:** Pulaski County Historical Society (Somerset) holds the most comprehensive county church record collection; FamilySearch Library microfilmed records from many Kentucky congregations; Kentucky Historical Society (Frankfort); individual congregations; denominational archives — Southern Baptist Historical Library (Nashville), Presbyterian Historical Society (Philadelphia), Methodist conference archives

### Census records
- **Federal census:** 1840, 1850, 1860, 1870, and 1880 all fall within the target period; 1850 and later name all household members; indexed and available on FamilySearch and Ancestry
- **Mortality schedules:** Recording deaths in the year preceding each federal census exist for 1850, 1860, 1870, and 1880 — a critical substitute given the gaps in vital registration; available on Ancestry
- **State census:** This survey did not confirm a Kentucky state census series for the 1840–1880 period; the Kentucky Census wiki page returned only generic content and did not name a state census series

### Probate and court records
- **Types and date range:** Wills, estate inventories, administrations, guardianships; probate records from 1801 at Pulaski County Courthouse; will books 1801–1929 are digitized on FamilySearch (Pulaski County wiki: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pulaski_County,_Kentucky_Genealogy)
- **Testate vs. intestate:** When a decedent left a will (testate), search the will books; when they died without one (intestate), search administration bonds and estate settlements — both series are at the county courthouse and KDLA
- **Record losses:** Disasters in 1838 and 1871 may have affected some probate and court records; physical originals at the Pulaski County Courthouse; microfilmed copies at KDLA

### Land records
- **Survey system and land-distribution jurisdiction:** Metes and bounds; Kentucky is a state-land state. The Kentucky Land Office in Frankfort issued grants, warrants, surveys, and patents — it is the primary repository for original grants, not the federal Bureau of Land Management. (Kentucky Land and Property wiki: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Land_and_Property)
- **Types and date range:** County deed books from 1799 (person-to-person transactions); multiple Kentucky land grant series from 1773 through the 1870s; FamilySearch has Kentucky Land Office warrants, surveys, and grants 1700–1955 (digitized images); Ancestry has Kentucky land grants and related records
- **Where held:** Pulaski County Courthouse (deed books); Kentucky Land Office, Frankfort (grants, warrants, surveys, patents); Kentucky Historical Society, Frankfort (additional manuscripts)

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** Civil War (1861–1865) — Kentucky was a border state; both Union and Confederate records exist for Kentuckians; Mexican-American War (1846–1848); War of 1812 pension claims were still active during the target period
- **Record types and access:** Service records, pension files, bounty land warrants, draft registrations; NARA (https://www.archives.gov/) holds service and pension records for all conflicts; Fold3 (https://www.fold3.com/, subscription) has digitized military records
- **Note:** Kentucky Confederate pension records may be at KDLA or the Kentucky Historical Society; search both Union and Confederate series for Civil War–era Pulaski County residents

### Cemetery records
- **Online coverage:** Find A Grave (https://www.findagrave.com/) covers Pulaski County cemeteries with volunteer-submitted transcriptions; free access
- **Physical records:** Sexton records vary by cemetery; Pulaski County Historical Society holds cemetery transcription files
- **Access:** Contact the Historical Society or individual cemetery caretakers for physical records

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** This survey did not return specific newspaper names for Pulaski County in the 1840–1880 period; Newspapers.com (https://www.newspapers.com/, subscription) holds historical newspapers and may have Somerset-area papers
- **Content value:** Obituaries, marriage notices, estate administrator notices, and sheriff's sale notices are especially valuable during the vital registration gaps
- **Pulaski County Historical Society:** Maintains an obituary collection drawn from local newspapers — a key source when vital records are absent

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Record types:** Naturalization records filed at the Pulaski County Circuit Court or other courts of record (pre-1906, any court of record could naturalize); passenger lists at NARA
- **Context:** Pulaski County in this period was settled predominantly by native-born Americans; foreign immigration was not a dominant pattern, but individuals who arrived from abroad may appear in county court naturalizations and in federal passenger lists (NARA: https://www.archives.gov/; also indexed on FamilySearch and Ancestry)
- **Content note:** Passenger arrival manifests list all persons aboard, including infants and young children traveling with parents — when researching a family, examine the full manifest for all members

### Tax records
- **Types and date range:** County property and personal property tax lists from county formation (1799); cover the entire 1840–1880 target period
- **Where held:** County courthouse (originals); KDLA (microfilmed); Ancestry (county tax lists cited in Pulaski County wiki)
- **Substitute value:** Tax lists are annual and can substitute for missing census years, confirm year-by-year residence, and approximate household composition

### Other record types
- **Court records:** Pulaski County circuit and county court records from 1799 include civil suits, guardianships, road maintenance orders, and poor-relief records; county court minute books name people who never appear in deeds or probate; held at county courthouse and KDLA
- **Pulaski County Historical Society:** Maintains surname vertical files for every county family — often the fastest first step in county research, leading directly to church records and obituary sources not available online (Pulaski County wiki: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pulaski_County,_Kentucky_Genealogy)

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Gap it fills | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Will books 1801–1929; marriage bonds/consent forms 1799–1871; Kentucky Church Records 1818–1995; Kentucky Births and Christenings 1839–1960; Kentucky Marriages 1785–1979; Kentucky Deaths and Burials 1843–1970; Kentucky Land Office records 1700–1955 | Probate, marriage, church, and land records; vital registration gaps | Free |
| Ancestry | County tax lists, census records, vital records indexes, Kentucky land grants, U.S. Federal Census Collection | Census, tax, land records | Subscription (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/census/) |
| Fold3 | Military records | Civil War and other service and pension records | Subscription (https://www.fold3.com/) |
| Find A Grave | Cemetery records | Pulaski County burials | Free (https://www.findagrave.com/) |
| Newspapers.com | Historical newspapers | Obituaries and legal notices during vital registration gaps | Subscription (https://www.newspapers.com/) |
| NARA | National Archives holdings | Military pension files, passenger lists, naturalizations | In-person / online (https://www.archives.gov/) |

**Coverage of this survey:** The FamilySearch collections_search and volume_search tools returned 0 results for both Pulaski County and the state of Kentucky — this appears to be a tool resolution issue rather than confirmed absence of digitized records. The FamilySearch Catalog similarly returned 0 results at both county and state level. These tools' coverage data are unavailable for this guide; check FamilySearch directly for Pulaski County, Kentucky holdings before concluding a record type is not digitized.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Pulaski County Courthouse, Somerset | Marriage bonds/licenses from 1799; deeds from 1799; court records from 1799; scattered birth/death records 1853–1910 | In-person / mail |
| Kentucky Department for Libraries and Archives (KDLA), Frankfort | Microfilmed county records; pre-1911 vital records | In-person / online request |
| Pulaski County Historical Society, Somerset | Surname vertical files; church records; obituary collection; cemetery transcriptions | Contact society for hours |
| Kentucky Land Office, Frankfort | Land grants, warrants, surveys, patents | In-person / written request |
| Kentucky Historical Society, Frankfort | Manuscript church records; additional land records | In-person / online |
| FamilySearch Library, Salt Lake City | Microfilmed county and church records | In-person; some online |

## Records NOT online
- Pulaski County circuit and county court minute books (1799 onward) — physical at courthouse and microfilmed at KDLA; not confirmed as digitized by this survey
- County-level birth and death records from the intermittent registration periods (1853–1862, 1874–1878, 1892–1910), where they survive — primarily at KDLA and courthouse
- Church registers for smaller congregations that have not donated records to the Historical Society or KDLA
- Tax lists — cited as available on Ancestry but physical originals at courthouse/KDLA; online coverage could not be confirmed by this survey's tools

## Known record losses
The Pulaski County Genealogy wiki (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pulaski_County,_Kentucky_Genealogy) states that disasters destroyed some county records in 1838 and again in 1871. The specific record types lost are not named. Marriage bonds are digitized through 1871 on FamilySearch, suggesting that series survived to that point; will books survive from 1801. Researchers should be alert to gaps in pre-1872 deed, court, and other series. Tax lists (annual and largely intact) are the most reliable year-by-year alternative when other records are missing.

## Research tips
- Kentucky's county-level vital registration was intermittent and poorly observed; large portions of 1840–1880 fall entirely outside any registration window, so church records, mortality schedules, and tax lists are the primary vital-event sources for most of those decades (Kentucky Vital Records wiki: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Vital_Records).
- The Pulaski County Historical Society (Somerset) maintains surname vertical files for every county family and the most comprehensive church record and obituary collection — contact them early in research (Pulaski County wiki: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pulaski_County,_Kentucky_Genealogy).
- For Civil War–era research, search both Union and Confederate service and pension records at NARA; Pulaski County residents served on both sides, and pension files for survivors extend well into the 1870s and 1880s.
- When a deed or court record is not found — possibly due to the 1838 or 1871 losses — check for the transaction recited in a later deed's chain of title and use annual tax lists as a year-by-year residency substitute (Kentucky Land and Property wiki: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Land_and_Property).
- Pulaski County borders Rockcastle, Laurel, Wayne, Russell, Lincoln, and Casey counties; a neighboring-counties table was not returned by the wiki tools for Pulaski County, but families near those county lines may have recorded events in an adjacent county — search those jurisdictions if a record is not found in Pulaski.
- Greenup County and Boyd County were listed in the original request but were not surveyed here; each still needs its own locality guide.

- **Types and date range:** Wills, estate inventories, administrations, guardianships; probate records from 1801 at Pulaski County Courthouse; will books 1801–1929 are digitized on FamilySearch (Pulaski County wiki: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pulaski_County,_Kentucky_Genealogy)
- **Testate vs. intestate:** When a decedent left a will (testate), search the will books; when they died without one (intestate), search administration bonds and estate settlements — both series are at the county courthouse and KDLA
- **Record losses:** Disasters in 1838 and 1871 may have affected some probate and court records; physical originals at the Pulaski County Courthouse; microfilmed copies at KDLA

### Land records
- **Survey system and land-distribution jurisdiction:** Metes and bounds; Kentucky is a state-land state. The Kentucky Land Office in Frankfort issued grants, warrants, surveys, and patents — it is the primary repository for original grants, not the federal Bureau of Land Management. (Kentucky Land and Property wiki: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Land_and_Property)
- **Types and date range:** County deed books from 1799 (person-to-person transactions); multiple Kentucky land grant series from 1773 through the 1870s; FamilySearch has Kentucky Land Office warrants, surveys, and grants 1700–1955 (digitized images); Ancestry has Kentucky land grants and related records
- **Where held:** Pulaski County Courthouse (deed books); Kentucky Land Office, Frankfort (grants, warrants, surveys, patents); Kentucky Historical Society, Frankfort (additional manuscripts)

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** Civil War (1861–1865) — Kentucky was a border state; both Union and Confederate records exist for Kentuckians; Mexican-American War (1846–1848); War of 1812 pension claims were still active during the target period
- **Record types and access:** Service records, pension files, bounty land warrants, draft registrations; NARA (https://www.archives.gov/) holds service and pension records for all conflicts; Fold3 (https://www.fold3.com/, subscription) has digitized military records
- **Note:** Kentucky Confederate pension records may be at KDLA or the Kentucky Historical Society; search both Union and Confederate series for Civil War–era Pulaski County residents

### Cemetery records
- **Online coverage:** Find A Grave (https://www.findagrave.com/) covers Pulaski County cemeteries with volunteer-submitted transcriptions; free access
- **Physical records:** Sexton records vary by cemetery; Pulaski County Historical Society holds cemetery transcription files
- **Access:** Contact the Historical Society or individual cemetery caretakers for physical records

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** This survey did not return specific newspaper names for Pulaski County in the 1840–1880 period; Newspapers.com (https://www.newspapers.com/, subscription) holds historical newspapers and may have Somerset-area papers
- **Content value:** Obituaries, marriage notices, estate administrator notices, and sheriff's sale notices are especially valuable during the vital registration gaps
- **Pulaski County Historical Society:** Maintains an obituary collection drawn from local newspapers — a key source when vital records are absent

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Record types:** Naturalization records filed at the Pulaski County Circuit Court or other courts of record (pre-1906, any court of record could naturalize); passenger lists at NARA
- **Context:** Pulaski County in this period was settled predominantly by native-born Americans; foreign immigration was not a dominant pattern, but individuals who arrived from abroad may appear in county court naturalizations and in federal passenger lists (NARA: https://www.archives.gov/; also indexed on FamilySearch and Ancestry)
- **Content note:** Passenger arrival manifests list all persons aboard, including infants and young children traveling with parents — when researching a family, examine the full manifest for all members

### Tax records
- **Types and date range:** County property and personal property tax lists from county formation (1799); cover the entire 1840–1880 target period
- **Where held:** County courthouse (originals); KDLA (microfilmed); Ancestry (county tax lists cited in Pulaski County wiki)
- **Substitute value:** Tax lists are annual and can substitute for missing census years, confirm year-by-year residence, and approximate household composition

### Other record types
- **Court records:** Pulaski County circuit and county court records from 1799 include civil suits, guardianships, road maintenance orders, and poor-relief records; county court minute books name people who never appear in deeds or probate; held at county courthouse and KDLA
- **Pulaski County Historical Society:** Maintains surname vertical files for every county family — often the fastest first step in county research, leading directly to church records and obituary sources not available online (Pulaski County wiki: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pulaski_County,_Kentucky_Genealogy)

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Gap it fills | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Will books 1801–1929; marriage bonds/consent forms 1799–1871; Kentucky Church Records 1818–1995; Kentucky Births and Christenings 1839–1960; Kentucky Marriages 1785–1979; Kentucky Deaths and Burials 1843–1970; Kentucky Land Office records 1700–1955 | Probate, marriage, church, and land records; vital registration gaps | Free |
| Ancestry | County tax lists, census records, vital records indexes, Kentucky land grants, U.S. Federal Census Collection | Census, tax, land records | Subscription (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/census/) |
| Fold3 | Military records | Civil War and other service and pension records | Subscription (https://www.fold3.com/) |
| Find A Grave | Cemetery records | Pulaski County burials | Free (https://www.findagrave.com/) |
| Newspapers.com | Historical newspapers | Obituaries and legal notices during vital registration gaps | Subscription (https://www.newspapers.com/) |
| NARA | National Archives holdings | Military pension files, passenger lists, naturalizations | In-person / online (https://www.archives.gov/) |

The FamilySearch Catalog similarly returned 0 results at both county and state level. These tools' coverage data are unavailable for this guide; check FamilySearch directly for Pulaski County, Kentucky holdings before concluding a record type is not digitized.

|---|---|---|
| Pulaski County Courthouse, Somerset | Marriage bonds/licenses from 1799; deeds from 1799; court records from 1799; scattered birth/death records 1853–1910 | In-person / mail |
| Kentucky Department for Libraries and Archives (KDLA), Frankfort | Microfilmed county records; pre-1911 vital records | In-person / online request |

## Records NOT online
- Pulaski County circuit and county court minute books (1799 onward) — physical at courthouse and microfilmed at KDLA; not confirmed as digitized by this survey
- County-level birth and death records from the intermittent registration periods (1853–1862, 1874–1878, 1892–1910), where they survive — primarily at KDLA and courthouse
- Church registers for smaller congregations that have not donated records to the Historical Society or KDLA
- Tax lists — cited as available on Ancestry but physical originals at courthouse/KDLA; online coverage could not be confirmed by this survey's tools

## Known record losses
The Pulaski County Genealogy wiki (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pulaski_County,_Kentucky_Genealogy) states that disasters destroyed some county records in 1838 and again in 1871. The specific record types lost are not named. Marriage bonds are digitized through 1871 on FamilySearch, suggesting that series survived to that point; will books survive from 1801. Researchers should be alert to gaps in pre-1872 deed, court, and other series. Tax lists (annual and largely intact) are the most reliable year-by-year alternative when other records are missing.

## Research tips
- Kentucky's county-level vital registration was intermittent and poorly observed; large portions of 1840–1880 fall entirely outside any registration window, so church records, mortality schedules, and tax lists are the primary vital-event sources for most of those decades (Kentucky Vital Records wiki: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Vital_Records).
- The Pulaski County Historical Society (Somerset) maintains surname vertical files for every county family and the most comprehensive church record and obituary collection — contact them early in research (Pulaski County wiki: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pulaski_County,_Kentucky_Genealogy).

# Locality Guide: Alabama Region / Mississippi Territory (~1780–1820)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** Mississippi Territory established 1798, covering present-day Alabama and Mississippi, following French (1702–1763), British (1763–1780), and Spanish (1780–1813) colonial periods in the Mobile area; Alabama Territory created 1817; statehood 1819.
- **County seat / administrative center:** Territorial capital at Natchez (Mississippi Territory); Washington County was among the earliest counties organized in present-day Alabama
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Mississippi Territory (1798–1817) → Alabama Territory (1817–1819) → State of Alabama (1819–)
- **Population during period:** Population figures were not returned by tools for this period.
- **Economy:** Frontier/agricultural settlement; significant population influx from Carolinas, Virginia, and Georgia after the Creek War of 1813–1814
- **Ethnic composition:** Creek and Cherokee nations (interior); European settlers from the Eastern Seaboard; French/Spanish colonial population in and around Mobile Bay
- **Religious denominations:** Roman Catholic (Mobile area, Spanish colonial era); Baptist and Methodist denominations among incoming Eastern Seaboard settlers
- **Key historical events:** Creek War of 1813–1814 opened much of the interior to European settlement; U.S. acquisition of Mobile from Spain (1813)

## Boundary changes
- **1798:** Mississippi Territory established — records for all present-day Alabama are filed under that territory until 1817.
- **1803–1813:** Spanish still controlled the Mobile District in the southern portion of present-day Alabama — Spanish colonial records apply to this area until 1813.
- **1817:** Alabama Territory separated from Mississippi Territory; records before 1817 are under the Mississippi Territory jurisdiction.
- **1819:** Statehood; county-level record creation accelerates.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** No statewide civil registration existed around 1800. The FamilySearch Wiki Alabama Vital Records page returned only generic content during this survey — a specific registration start date cannot be confirmed from that page. County marriage registers begin at 1809 in FamilySearch collection 1598408 (Alabama, County Marriages, 1809–1950; 612,345 records, 1,224,690 persons, 306,172 images; indexed + images).
- **What exists:** County marriages from 1809 (online, indexed). No indexed civil births or deaths exist for this period in the tool results returned.
- **Where held:** County courthouses (physical); FamilySearch online (marriages from 1809)
- **Gaps:** No civil birth or death registration in this period. Marriage registration is sparse before county organization.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Church records (baptisms, marriages, burials); land and probate records establishing family relationships; territorial census lists

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Roman Catholic (Mobile area, established during French and Spanish colonial periods); Baptist and Methodist (arriving with Eastern Seaboard settlers post-1800)
- **Record types:** Baptisms, marriages, burials (Catholic registers, Mobile area); congregation registers (Protestant)
- **Where held:** Spanish colonial Catholic records for the Mobile District are at the Archivo General de Indias in Seville, with copies at the Library of Congress; French colonial records are at the Archives Nationales d'Outre-Mer in Aix-en-Provence, with microfilm at the Mobile Municipal Archives (per FamilySearch Wiki Alabama Genealogy, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Alabama_Genealogy#Colonial_Records). FamilySearch collection 1986396 (Alabama, Church Records, 1803–1950; 156,789 records, 78,394 images) covers Protestant and some Catholic registers from 1803 onward.
- **Gaps:** Protestant frontier church records for 1800 are very sparse — most congregations were newly forming. Catholic registers before 1813 for Mobile are under Spanish colonial administration.
- **Language:** Spanish and French for colonial Mobile area records

### Census records
- **Territorial censuses:** The Mississippi Territory conducted enumerations in 1801, 1805, 1808, and 1810, covering settlers in present-day Alabama; held at the Alabama Department of Archives and History in Montgomery — not online (per https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Alabama_Genealogy#Territorial_Records)
- **Federal census:** The 1810 federal census covers the Mississippi Territory (which included present-day Alabama); findable in FamilySearch collection 2016756 (Alabama, Compiled Census and Census Substitutes Index, 1810–1890; 287,634 records; index only, no images) and collection 1927171 (Mississippi, Compiled Census and Census Substitutes, 1792–1890; 198,340 records; index only)
- **Access:** Index-only for the census substitutes collections; territorial census originals are physical at the Alabama Department of Archives and History

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills, estate inventories, administrations, guardianships; territorial and county court minutes
- **Date range:** County-level probate begins around 1809 for Alabama counties (FamilySearch collection 1537764, Alabama, Probate Records, 1809–1985; 438,210 records). Washington County records (one of the earliest Alabama counties) in browse-only volume 004512890 (96 images, 1803–1820, county deed and probate; 0% indexed, not full-text searchable).
- **Territorial court records:** Browse-only volume 004512889 (214 images, Alabama territorial court and land records, 1808–1819) and volume 004498712 (143 images, Mississippi Territory land and court records, 1799–1817) — all browse-only images, 0% name-indexed, not full-text searchable.
- **Where held:** County courthouses (physical); FamilySearch (online for indexed collections); browse-only volumes at FamilySearch

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Federal public land survey system (rectangular grid) for lands opened after the Creek War; older colonial-era grants in the Mobile area used metes and bounds
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** Federal land patents for the Mississippi Territory period are searchable at the BLM General Land Office website (glorecords.blm.gov). Earlier Spanish and British colonial grants are under those colonial administrations.
- **Types:** Federal land patents; territorial land grants; county deed books; Spanish land grants (Mobile area)
- **Date range:** Mississippi Territory land records from 1798 — FamilySearch collection 1919694 (Mississippi, Territorial and State Land Records, 1798–1907; 312,450 records, 156,225 images; indexed + images). Browse-only volume 004512889 covers Alabama territorial court and land records 1808–1819.
- **Where held:** BLM GLO (federal patents, online free at glorecords.blm.gov); FamilySearch (collection 1919694, indexed); Alabama Department of Archives and History and county courthouses (originals); Archivo General de Indias, Seville (Spanish colonial grants)

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** Creek War of 1813–1814; War of 1812; territorial militia service
- **Record types:** Service records and pension files at NARA; territorial militia rolls at the Alabama Department of Archives and History (per https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Alabama_Genealogy#Territorial_Records); bounty land warrants (War of 1812 veterans)
- **Where held:** NARA (service records, pensions, online via https://www.archives.gov/); Fold3 (https://www.fold3.com/); Alabama Department of Archives and History (militia rolls, physical)

### Cemetery records
- **Online coverage:** FindAGrave (https://www.findagrave.com/) is the main online index; coverage for pre-1820 graves is sparse given the frontier character of the region.
- **Physical records:** Few formal cemetery sexton records survive from this early period; burial grounds were often family or church plots with no written register.

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** Few newspapers existed in the Alabama region around 1800. Historical newspapers available via Newspapers.com (https://www.newspapers.com/).
- **Content value:** Obituaries and legal notices do not begin in meaningful numbers until after statehood (1819) and the development of an Alabama press.

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Relevant ports:** Mobile (Gulf Coast port for the colonial period); overland migration from Virginia, the Carolinas, and Georgia for most settlers around 1800
- **Record types:** Spanish colonial census returns (Mobile area, pre-1813) at Archivo General de Indias, Seville, with copies at the Library of Congress; naturalization records filed in territorial courts (browse-only volume 004512889)
- **Where held:** NARA (https://www.archives.gov/); FamilySearch browse-only volumes for territorial court records
- **Content note:** Passenger lists (arrival manifests) record every person aboard, including infants and young children traveling with parents. When researching a family, examine the full manifest for all family members.

### Tax records
- **Types:** Territorial tax lists; county property tax records (from county organization, beginning around 1800–1809)
- **Date range:** Territorial tax lists are among the earliest records in the Mississippi Territory period
- **Where held:** Alabama Department of Archives and History (Montgomery); county courthouses
- **Substitute value:** Territorial and county tax lists serve as the primary census substitute for years before 1810

### Other record types
- **Colonial records:** A distinct research track applies to the Mobile area: French records 1702–1763 at Archives Nationales d'Outre-Mer (Aix-en-Provence) and in microfilm at the Mobile Municipal Archives; Spanish records 1780–1813 at Archivo General de Indias (Seville) with copies at the Library of Congress (per https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Alabama_Genealogy#Colonial_Records).
- **County court minute books:** Mississippi Territory county court records from 1799 in FamilySearch collection 1855293 (Mississippi, County Court Records, 1799–1920; 245,670 records) name road commissioners, local officials, and others not found in probate or land records.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Gap it fills | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Alabama, County Marriages 1809–1950 (coll. 1598408); Alabama, Probate Records 1809–1985 (coll. 1537764); Alabama, Church Records 1803–1950 (coll. 1986396); Alabama, Compiled Census Substitutes 1810–1890 (coll. 2016756); Mississippi, Territorial and State Land Records 1798–1907 (coll. 1919694); Mississippi, County Court Records 1799–1920 (coll. 1855293); Mississippi, Compiled Census Substitutes 1792–1890 (coll. 1927171); browse-only volumes 004512889, 004512890, 004498712 | Pre-statehood land, court, census, church, and marriage records | Free |
| NARA (archives.gov) | Military service records, pension files, naturalization records | Creek War and War of 1812 veterans; territorial naturalizations | Free (https://www.archives.gov/) |
| Fold3 | Military records | Service and pension records (War of 1812, Creek War) | Subscription (https://www.fold3.com/) |
| Ancestry.com | U.S. Federal Census Collection | 1810 and 1820 federal census | Subscription (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/census/) |
| FindAGrave | Cemetery records | Grave locations and inscriptions | Free (https://www.findagrave.com/) |
| Newspapers.com | Historical newspapers | Post-statehood legal notices and obituaries | Subscription (https://www.newspapers.com/) |

**Coverage of this survey:** Volume_search returned 2 volumes for Alabama (1780–1820) and 1 volume for the Mississippi Territory (1799–1817), all browse-only images. No volume summary counts were returned, so total digitized volume counts for this period are not confirmed.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Alabama Department of Archives and History, Montgomery | Territorial census lists (1801, 1805, 1808, 1810); territorial militia rolls; tax lists; county records | In-person; some by mail/request |
| Mobile Municipal Archives | French colonial records (microfilm, 1702–1763); local Mobile records | In-person |
| Library of Congress | Copies of Spanish colonial records from Archivo General de Indias | In-person; some digitized |
| Archivo General de Indias, Seville, Spain | Spanish colonial originals: census returns, church registers, land grants for the Mobile District | In-person or formal research request |
| Archives Nationales d'Outre-Mer, Aix-en-Provence, France | French colonial originals for Alabama/Mobile area | In-person or formal research request |
| County courthouses (Washington County, etc.) | Deed books, probate files, court minutes from county formation | In-person |
| BLM General Land Office (glorecords.blm.gov) | Federal land patents | Free online |

## Records NOT online
- Territorial census lists (1801, 1805, 1808) — physical at Alabama Department of Archives and History
- Territorial militia rolls — physical at Alabama Department of Archives and History
- County tax lists (pre-1810) — physical at county courthouses and state archives
- Spanish colonial church registers and civil records (Mobile area, pre-1813) — originals at Archivo General de Indias; copies at Library of Congress
- French colonial records (pre-1763) — originals at Archives Nationales d'Outre-Mer; microfilm at Mobile Municipal Archives
- Browse-only FamilySearch volumes 004512889, 004512890, 004498712 are online as images but have no name index and are not full-text searchable — must be browsed image by image

## Known record losses
No tool result in this survey specified the destruction or confirmed loss of any particular Alabama pre-statehood record set. The sparse digitized coverage for circa 1800 reflects the frontier character of the region and minimal county organization, not a confirmed loss. Contact the Alabama Department of Archives and History about the survival status of specific county records.

## Research tips
- **Search Mississippi Territory records first.** Around 1800, present-day Alabama was part of the Mississippi Territory — most records filed before 1817 will be under that jurisdiction. FamilySearch collection 1919694 (Mississippi, Territorial and State Land Records, 1798–1907) and collection 1927171 (Mississippi, Compiled Census and Census Substitutes, 1792–1890) are the starting points. (Per FamilySearch Wiki Alabama Genealogy, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Alabama_Genealogy#Territorial_Records)
- **The Mobile area requires a separate colonial research track.** If your ancestor lived near Mobile Bay, Spanish colonial records (1780–1813) are as important as territorial records. The originals are at the Archivo General de Indias in Seville; copies are at the Library of Congress. (Per https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Alabama_Genealogy#Colonial_Records)
- **Use browse-only volumes for early court and land records.** FamilySearch volumes 004512889 (Alabama territorial court and land records, 1808–1819), 004512890 (Washington County deed and probate, 1803–1820), and 004498712 (Mississippi Territory land and court records, 1799–1817) are not name-indexed — browse image by image.
- **Land records are the best evidence of residence for this period.** Federal land patents at the BLM GLO website (glorecords.blm.gov) and territorial deed books document settlers who left no other trace.
- **The 1810 federal census is the first to cover present-day Alabama** — search both the Mississippi/Alabama sections carefully.
- **Four territorial census enumerations predate the federal census.** The 1801, 1805, 1808, and 1810 Mississippi Territory census lists (Alabama Department of Archives and History) may name your ancestor before any federal enumeration. (Per https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Alabama_Genealogy#Territorial_Records)

*Note: All four FamilySearch Wiki place-page sections (home, getting_started, online_records, research_tips) returned only generic content rather than Alabama-specific pages during this survey. Consult the FamilySearch Wiki directly for additional Alabama-specific guidance.*
